date_note: Elliptic's page was first published on 3 November and has been updated since; the 23 November version gave 3,930 BTC ($247 million), the 26 November version gives 6,330 BTC ($389 million).
title: Elliptic: at least 6,330 BTC ($389 million) from the Binance theft has gone into coinjoins since November 1
summary: Elliptic's page, last updated 26 November, says at least 6,330 BTC ($389 million) of the funds stolen from Binance has gone into coinjoins since November 1. Its 23 November version said it tracks more than 27,000 wallets on at least 16 blockchains and that the laundering may involve Chinese money laundering networks. Elliptic says the laundering is clearly automated but nothing it has seen shows an AI agent making decisions.
plain: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic says at least 6,330 BTC ($389 million) of the money stolen from Binance has been put through mixing transactions since November 1.
exec: Elliptic reports at least 6,330 BTC ($389 million) of Binance theft proceeds has been mixed since November 1, which complicates tracing and recovery.

evidence.quote: In total, at least 6,330 BTC ($389 million) has now gone into coinjoins since November 1.
using more than 27,000 wallets on at least 16 blockchains, about 55 services and about 90,000 transactions

validation.note: Elliptic's own report is the primary source; Bitcoin.com News (Jamie Redman, 23 Nov) relays it and adds Elliptic co-founder Tom Robinson's LinkedIn remark that the China link is not conclusive. The PANews item cites CoinDesk, which was not read.

review.note: 6,330 BTC, 27,000 wallets, AI-agent line, update date checked against Elliptic; possible-duplicate with Lookonchain ETH event is a different event

key_findings: Elliptic says the Binance theft of 29 October was a multi-stage campaign in which attackers gained access through compromised tools and fake job interviews.
It says laundering spans more than 27,000 wallets, 16 blockchains and about 55 services.
Elliptic says stolen funds are being converted to bitcoin and increasingly mixed through coinjoins, Privacy Cash and Tornado Cash, and that most have not been cashed out.
It says the laundering appears automated but it found no evidence of AI agents making decisions.
recommendations: Screen against the linked addresses; Elliptic offers a free Binance-hack blocklist.
Elliptic also suggests its Fast Track Monitoring service as a backup screening option.

links.rel: Elliptic's coinjoin tracing cited in the Reuters report
